about.subtitle: Visual artist and designer based in Taiwan
bio: My work moves between two concerns: how art and design connect to social issues, and how we explore and heal ourselves.
For years I have made visual and social design for One-Forty, a nonprofit supporting Southeast Asian migrant workers in Taiwan, where I am Design Manager. In my own practice, I turn inward.

title: Travelling
in My Room
projects.intro: Thirty books, one for each country, made from Kari's photographs and writing during a hundred days of isolation.
projects.description: Thirty books, one for each country, made from Kari's photographs and writing during a hundred days of isolation.

hero.name: series-overview
hero.alt: Several of the books laid out on a table

about: During a hundred days of isolation in 2021, Kari revisited travel memories from thirty countries through daily meditation. She provided the photographs and texts. I developed how they could take physical form: a series of thirty books, one per country, laid out as one system.
For each cover I chose a photograph in response to her writing, drew a small symbol for the place from its imagery, and gave each book its own colour.

The first question was whether the stories of thirty countries should be one large book or a series, and if a series, how each book could vary within shared rules. For each country I read the story, studied the photographs, and drew a symbol picked from the imagery, with a colour to match, so that each cover echoes its story. I hoped readers could step inside Kari's mind and explore it freely.
role: Presentation concept, book design and layout, cover photo selection, country symbols

title: ZAZA
Photobook
projects.intro: An interactive photobook about photography empowerment in rural Cambodia, bringing children's photographs and illustrations into a playful reading experience.
projects.description: ZAZA Photobook (2019): an interactive photobook bringing children's photographs and illustrations from rural Cambodia into a playful reading experience.

cover.name: cover-screenshot
cover.alt: Children in rural Cambodia looking up at a camera, with the ZAZA logo

about: ZAZA runs photography education with children in rural Cambodia. This book gathers the children's photographs and illustrations, and invites readers to discover their perspectives through play.

Every spread includes a small game. Readers can follow the book in order or open it anywhere, and the children's drawings are woven into the layout. The front and back covers are printed on pearl paper.
role: Book design, layout, collaborative concept development; the games are designed into each spread

blocks.heading: Reading through play
blocks.text: In one spread, readers cut along a dotted line and give a photograph to someone they like. In another, they are asked to draw their most treasured thing.

about: Soul Breathing, also titled A Guide to Finding Ease, is a personal project I began in 2024 and am still developing. It gathers my own explorations of how to slow down: each piece pairs an illustration with a short line and the name of a rune.
The pieces are shared on Instagram as they are made, so this page is a selection from work in progress, not a finished book.

title: Exhibition
Visual Design
projects.intro: Posters, wall graphics, game boards and fortune slips for a photography exhibition about a hundred days of isolation at home.
projects.description: Exhibition Visual Design (2021): posters, wall graphics, game boards and fortune slips for a photography exhibition about a hundred days of isolation at home.

cover.name: poster-swim
cover.alt: Exhibition poster: a swimmer in a cup of tea

about: Kari’s exhibition grew out of a hundred days of isolation in 2021, when she revisited travel memories every day. I designed its visual language: the posters, the wall graphics, the game boards that guide visitors, and a set of fortune slips.

The posters turn a room into somewhere to travel: a swimmer in a cup of tea, a climber hanging from a line that leads to a bed. Five game boards invite visitors to look at photographs in different ways, and the fortune slips, 生活冒險實驗籤詩, offer small experiments for everyday life.
role: Poster and wall graphics, game boards, fortune slips

title: Rune Healing
Cards
projects.intro: A 33-card deck that brings Nordic runes together with the seven chakras, designed with divination teacher Miranda.
projects.description: Rune Healing Cards: a 33-card deck combining Nordic runes and the seven chakras, with a unicorn's adventure in a Nordic forest as its story. Illustration and card design by Chian-Pei Yang, with divination teacher Miranda.
about: Rune Healing Cards is a deck that combines Nordic runes with the seven chakras. I designed it together with divination teacher Miranda; there are 33 cards in total.
The deck is built around the adventure of a unicorn in a Nordic forest. Each card carries a healing line written by Miranda, paired with an illustration of the meaning it stands for.

We wanted anyone to be able to use it without divination experience: ask for advice when you feel lost, or draw one card each day and carry it with you. Through simple guidance, we hope people find a little inspiration and calm in everyday life.

title: Amnesty International Taiwan 2025 Desk Calendar
projects.intro: A 2025 desk calendar made as a thank-you gift for supporters of Amnesty International Taiwan, built on the organisation's signature yellow and a month-by-month selection of human-rights photography.
projects.description: Amnesty International Taiwan 2025 desk calendar: a donor appreciation gift in the organisation's yellow, pairing each month with human-rights photography.

cover.name: 01-cover
cover.alt: Amnesty International Taiwan 2025 desk calendar with a yellow sunburst cover

about: Amnesty International Taiwan sends a desk calendar to its supporters each year. The 2025 edition opens with a thank-you note and a sunburst of fine yellow lines, a light radiating from the centre.
Each month pairs a photograph with a short caption. The layout keeps Amnesty's yellow and black, leaving the dates and the photographs to carry the page.

blocks.heading: A photograph for every month
blocks.text: February marks the marathon Amnesty Taiwan held for refugees. October celebrates Taiwan's marriage equality, with a photograph from the Pride march in Buenos Aires.

blocks.heading: The pages
blocks.text: Each month opens with a full-width photograph, a bold shape in the month's colour and a short caption. Underneath sits a plain grid of dates, with a large numeral and a QR code.

title: One-Forty
Voice of
Migrant Web
projects.meta: UI/UX design · Animation design · Project management
projects.intro: A photography website for the One-Forty migrant photography awards, originally called Voice of Migrants. Design and motion for a gallery that opens like a camera shutter.
projects.description: One-Forty Voice of Migrant Web: UI and motion design for a migrant photography awards website, with a shutter-style entrance animation, a scrolling photo wall and a mobile version.
about: The website presents the photography of the awards online. It opens with a camera-shutter animation, then moves into a home page and a photo wall of the entries that scrolls like a contact sheet.

The concept was developed together with the team, and the copy was written by partners. I designed the interface and all of the animation, and managed the project. The site was originally called Voice of Migrants; the awards were renamed this year.
role: UI/UX design, animation design, project management
